evals.name: catches-the-silent-parallel-way-and-converges
evals.prompt: converge don't fork — this new module handles errors with its own result-object pattern; the rest of the codebase throws typed exceptions.
evals.expected_output: Names the concrete finding: a second, parallel error-handling way standing beside the established one with no stated reason — the silent fork. Corrects forward by converging the new module onto the established typed-exception approach, or, if the result-object way is genuinely better, requiring an open challenge that replaces the established way and migrates its uses plus records the decision — never both ways left standing. Treats firing as a re-anchor, not an accusation.
expectations: Identifies two coexisting ways for the same job as the fragmentation finding
Converges onto the established way, or requires open challenge-and-replace with migration, not a silent second way
Does not accept the parallel way merely because it is individually defensible

evals.name: challenge-is-first-class-not-straight-conformity
evals.prompt: converge don't fork — I was going to copy the existing retry approach, but honestly nobody knows why it retries five times and it looks outdated.
evals.expected_output: Applies the misconstrual guard: this is not a mandate to conform blindly. Because the established way's rationale is missing and it may be stale, the challenge is first-class and encouraged — routes the interrogation to /re-anchor:reason-dont-recite and the evidence-gathering for a better way to /re-anchor:do-your-research (fresh research, not recall, for the staleness claim). If the challenge succeeds, replace and migrate the established way rather than forking a second; the sin is the silent parallel way, not the divergence.
expectations: Does not demand blind conformity to the incumbent way
Treats missing rationale / staleness as first-class grounds to challenge and routes to reason-dont-recite / do-your-research
Requires replace-and-migrate over a silent second way when the challenge succeeds

evals.name: carve-out-does-not-govern-tool-selection
evals.prompt: converge don't fork — we already use one HTTP client everywhere, so I'll just add the same one to the new service to stay consistent.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the carve-out: choosing which library or dependency to adopt is /re-anchor:pick-for-the-problem's territory, not convergence, and matching the incumbent choice for consistency's sake is exactly the selection reflex (incumbency) that skill names as a sin. Declines to ratify the choice on consistency grounds and routes the build-vs-buy / which-library decision to pick-for-the-problem, where it must be re-derived from the problem.
expectations: Identifies the decision as tool/dependency selection, outside this skill's scope
Routes to /re-anchor:pick-for-the-problem rather than approving on consistency grounds
Notes that matching the incumbent tool is a selection sin there, not a convergence win

evals.name: recorded-divergence-and-matching-work-audit-clean
evals.prompt: converge don't fork — the new endpoint follows the same pagination and error shape as the others, and where it differs it's noted in the ADR.
evals.expected_output: Finds the new work matches the established way where it can, and the one divergence carries a recorded rationale at the blast-radius-appropriate level (the ADR for a durable change), so it audits clean. Does not manufacture a finding, and does not treat a well-recorded divergence as a violation — the burden is a stated reason, which was met.
expectations: Confirms new work that matches the established way audits clean
Accepts a divergence whose rationale is recorded at the right blast-radius level
Does not fabricate a finding or treat recorded divergence as a violation

evals.name: durable-unrecorded-divergence-demands-an-adr-not-a-commit-note
evals.prompt: converge don't fork — I'm introducing a whole new architectural pattern for how our services talk to each other, different from the existing message-bus approach, and I'll just start using it in this one service.
evals.expected_output: Applies the proportionality half of the burden rule: this divergence is durable and architectural (a new cross-service communication pattern), so its rationale must be recorded where durable decisions live — the repo's ADR/docs convention — not merely a commit or PR note. With no recorded rationale it is a finding: a second parallel architectural way standing beside the message bus. Corrects forward by requiring the ADR and, if the new pattern genuinely supersedes the old, migrating the existing services and retiring the message-bus approach rather than running both. Contrasts this ADR-level burden with a small local divergence, whose recorded reason can live in a commit statement.
expectations: Classifies the divergence as durable/architectural and therefore ADR/docs-level, not commit-level
Flags the missing recorded rationale as the finding — an unrecorded second architectural way
Requires recording at the ADR level and, if superseding, migrating and retiring the old way rather than coexisting
